title: Token cost ledger ingestion spec and trace grafting
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define and implement a lightweight ingestion pipeline that binds per-token timing probes to a persistent cost ledger and grafts trace spans so downstream billing and SLA dashboards can attribute latency/cost to individual tokens and cache events. Deliverables: ingestion spec, trace-grafting library, sample dashboard panels, and a low-overhead rollout plan.
implementation_notes: Goal is O(1) extra ms and <5% p99 token path overhead when sampling at 10%
Use probabilistic sampling at the ingress router and deterministic sampling keys to join traces with ledger rows
Ledger rows are compact (proto) with fields: request_id, token_index, microseconds, kv_hit_flag, model_variant, kernel_profile
Trace grafting implemented as a middleware that attaches a synthetic token-span with tags for billing ledgers to the request-parent span
Storage: short-term streaming store (ksql/kafka topic + consumer) writes to ledger table in ClickHouse for aggregation queries
Expose join keys to the console via trace id -> ledger row mapping API with 24h retention for initial rollout
